label: Encoded origin-tolerance countermodel checked
description: The five-world Control.faithful satisfies all four encoded origin commitments and every premise of ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete except Euclidean access at actual, while that frame condition and the conclusion fail there. This is a nonvacuous countermodel to omission for exactly that bundle. Individual b is necessary relative to plus but absent from aMinus, which actual accesses and plus does not; individual a is contingent relative to plus. The separate restored conjunct checks one three-offset assignment with its only individual at every world, so the arrival conclusion holds there; it proves no general claim about restoring origins. Unregistered deduction from the existing earlierNecessary theorem: the temporal premises already require an individual necessary at the temporal witness and a distinct contingent individual, so those premises have no one-individual model. This does not render the existing two-individual model vacuous. Direct evaluation, not a new certificate conjunct: both actual individuals can be deleted separately at accessible worlds (a at bMinus, b at aMinus). Requiring such deletion at every world instead contradicts earlierNecessary under presence-to-existence, inert emptiness and the possible contingent-free past. That is incompatibility of a stronger bundle, not failure of this original model or independent warrant for the added deletion premise. Scope: faithful only to the encoded analyst commitments (rigid identity; access iff shared individuals have near origins, whose if-half remains OPEN; near-origin plenitude; one varied individual), with stipulated absences and a temporal profile not tied to origins. No counterpart, vague or kind-relative account or unrestricted recombination principle is certified. Individual deletion at actual and the stronger worldwise-deletion objection are evaluated separately in the linked attempt; neither is a conjunct of this certificate.

research_comparisons.conditions: Near is a tolerance, origin plenitude and a varied individual at actual hold together with reflexivity at actual, presence-to-existence, inert emptiness and the possible contingent-free past in Control.faithful.
research_comparisons.scope: Same Frame, Ontic and History carrier as ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete; five worlds, two rigidly identified individuals, three origin offsets, natural-number times, selected world World.actual.
research_comparisons.coverage: One finite origin-tolerance encoding with rigid identity and a three-value origin space; not counterpart, vague-tolerance or kind-relative accounts, and not the possible-external-cause arrival.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: With the varied individual and near a tolerance, origin-determined access entails the negation of Euclidean access at actual (originToleranceNonEuclidean).
research_comparisons.witness: Control.faithful, the first two conjunct groups of Control.Certificate (encoded commitments only, with stipulated absences and temporal profile); a is absent from bMinus and b from aMinus, so NecessaryConcreteAt fails at actual.
research_comparisons.next_step: Assess independent warrant for a cross-world persistence or worldwise-deletion bridge while preserving the original countermodel; actual-only deletion is already compatible with it. The possible-external-cause arrival remains untested.
